requirements_summary: Repo-aware code assistant: need repository-level embeddings + vector DB that can be VPC-hosted or fully on-prem. Workloads: low-latency code completion + multi-file code search. Targets: token-level streaming under 50ms median for warmed contexts, 200 QPS overall for completions, 5k QPS for embeddings indexing during reindex windows. Prefer model pinning for deterministic behavior (no continuous weights drift). Chunking: language-aware chunker (function/class boundaries), configurable overlap (10-20%); deduping. Vector store: must support residency (on-prem or VPC subnet), incremental upserts, TTL controls, multi-tenancy isolation. Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2 baseline, KMS integration for keys, audit logs, retention controls and explicit statement that code does not leave customer-managed network without consent.
notes: POC notes / sales log: short, choppy - CTO (Maya Patel) quote: 'If code leaves our network we won't sign — residency is non-negotiable.' They want repo-aware retrieval (not just README-level). POC ran against mono-repo + microservice repos. Tried two approaches: 1) file-level chunks with syntactic boundaries (better precision), 2) sliding-window tokens (higher recall). Results: file-level gave fewer false positives in 'go-to-definition' style queries. Using pgvector in VPC for POC; customer wants option to host vector DB on-prem behind HSM. Embeddings candidates discussed: code-focused embed model vs general text embed; they saw ~8% higher recall with code-tuned vectors. Chunk size experiments: 256-512 tokens optimal for functions, 1024 for docs. Asked about continuous batching and prefix caching to hit sub-50ms: Diego demoed prefix/KV-cache reuse and streaming options — CX liked it but legal asked for a written latency SLA. Model/version pinning: must be able to pin to a named artifact and lock quantization profile. They asked about fallback routing to smaller models for degraded capacity; prefer deterministic fallback list. Cost sensitivity: mid-market price expectations; will accept hosted during dev but must move to private for prod. Next: security wants drive docs (sent), legal wants specific egress clause. Sales notes: prepare two pricing rows: hosted dev + private prod with on-prem vector store. Potential upsell: Redwood Optimize for batching/quant recommendations.
